data.description:
Churn is the percentage of paid subscriptions that were lost during a given period.

Actives measures the number of paid subscriptions at the beginning of a a given period, while Churned Actives measures the paid subscriptions that have expired within the period.

A stable or declining churn rate indicates a healthy, growing business. However, keep in mind that churn can be relatively high for mobile apps when compared to web SaaS products.

measures.description: The number of un-expired subscriptions at the beginning of the period.
The number of subscriptions that expired in the period and did not renew.
The proportion of subscriptions active at the beginning of the period that expired in the period and did not renew.

data.description:
Initial conversion measures what proportion of new customers start any subscription (including trial) or make any purchase.

Since this chart is cohorted by the earliest date that a customer was first seen by RevenueCat (e.g. when they first opened the app, or when they first made a purchase outside of the app), each period measures the number of New Customers first seen in that period, and the number of those customers that have converted on any product (Initial Conversions). For apps that exclusively rely on products with trials, the initial conversion rate is equal to the trial start rate. For apps that offer no trials at all, the initial conversion rate is equal to the conversion rate to paying (because there are no subscribers that don't pay).

The conversion timeframe selector sets the maximum amount of time each period's cohort has to convert within for accurate historical comparisons.

measures.description: The number of new customers that were first seen during the cohort period.
The number of customers that converted to any purchase (including regular subscriptions but also trial starts, intro periods, and non-renewing IAPs) within 7 days of when they were first seen.
The percentage of customers that have converted into any purchase within 7 days of when they were first seen.

data.description:
Conversion to Paying measures what proportion of new customers make any payment.

Since this chart is cohorted by the earliest date that a customer was first seen by RevenueCat (e.g. when they first opened the app, or when they first made a purchase outside of the app), each period measures the number of New Customers first seen in that period, and the number of those customers that are now Paying Customers.

The conversion timeframe selector sets the maximum amount of time each period's cohort has to convert within for accurate historical comparisons.

measures.description: The number of new customers that were first seen during the cohort period.
The number of customers that converted to a paid purchase (including subscriptions not in their trial period as well as non-renewing IAPs) within 7 days of when they were first seen.
The percentage of customers that have converted to a paid purchase within 7 days of when they were first seen.

data.description:
Subscription Retention measures how paying subscriptions renew and retain over time by cohorts.

When segmenting by subscription start date, cohorts are segmented by the start of a paid subscription. Subsequent periods along the horizontal table indicate how many subscriptions continued renewing through those periods. When segmenting by other fields, cohorts are segmented by the values within that field, and include all paid subscriptions started within the specified date range. Subsequent periods along the horizontal table indicate the portion of subscriptions that successfully renewed out of all those that had the opportunity to renew in a given period.

The final, incomplete period is indicated with a hashed background and shows how many subscriptions are set to renew by the end of the period, taking into account the auto-renewal preference of the subscriptions.
